name: com.easycando/easycando
title: EasyCanDo
description: Search a checked catalog of 1,300 AI models, APIs, data feeds and apps by what each takes and gives.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Find tools in the EasyCanDo catalog for one step of a build. Give a short query saying what the step does, and have and want when you know what goes in and what should come out. Returns up to 10 previews, best first: slug, one-line summary, the capability that matched with its input and output types, API status, price tier, the date it was checked and page URL, plus the arguments for the next page. Call get_tool before writing integration code.

query.description: What the step does, in a few words: “transcribe audio”, “vector database”, “send sms”.

have.description: What the step starts with. One of: words (words: text, query, message, social-post); photos (photos and images: image, image-mask, 3d); video (video: video); sound (voice and sound: audio-speech, audio, audio-music, audio-sfx); documents (documents: document); links (web links: url, webpage); places (places: geo); data (numbers and data: structured, timeseries, event-stream, embedding); code (code: code); money (money: money); people (people: profile); dates (dates and events: schedule). A type id in parentheses also works, and stands for the id before it.

want.description: What the step should produce. One of: words (words: text, query, message, social-post); photos (photos and images: image, image-mask, 3d); video (video: video); sound (voice and sound: audio-speech, audio, audio-music, audio-sfx); documents (documents: document); links (web links: url, webpage); places (places: geo); data (numbers and data: structured, timeseries, event-stream, embedding); code (code: code); money (money: money); people (people: profile); dates (dates and events: schedule); done (something done: action:publish, action:message, action:money, action:world, action:software, action:browser, action:schedule, action:record, physical-item). A type id in parentheses also works, and stands for the id before it. “done” means the tool acts: it posts, sends, pays, books or changes something.

free.description: Only tools that are free or have a free tier.

local.description: Only tools that run on the user’s own machine.

live.description: Only tools with live or real-time data.

official.description: Only tools with an official API.

group.description: Only one group. One of: images (make, edit and fix pictures); video (make and edit video, avatars and 3d); voice (speak, transcribe, compose and clean up sound); design (make documents, slides and designs); ai (language models and agents that think and act); reading (read text out of pages, photos, audio and video); web (search the web and follow the news); social (read what people post and say); knowledge (papers, books, records and public data); world (weather, sky, earth, flights and places); posting (publish posts and send messages); money (markets, payments, stores and ads); home (lights, devices, deliveries and real things); mac (tools that run on your own mac, so nothing leaves it); building (code, data, hosting and the parts apps are made of).

offset.description: Results to skip. Use the next-page arguments a search returns.

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: Get the full record of up to 5 tools: each capability with its input and output types, price and limits; API status, sign-up and auth; price tier and free tier; ways in (web API, SDKs, official MCP); docs, pricing and site links; terms; ranking; and the date it was checked. Takes slugs from search_tools, page URLs or tool names. Call it before writing integration code.

slugs.description: 1 to 5 tools: slugs from search_tools, easycando.com page URLs or tool names.

tools.name: find_chains
tools.description: Find tools that turn one kind of input into another: single tools that do it in one capability, and chains of two tools in a row with the type passed between them. Use it when search_tools finds no single tool for a step. Give a query saying what the chain is for, so the best chains come first.

have.description: What the step starts with. One of: words (words: text, query, message, social-post); photos (photos and images: image, image-mask, 3d); video (video: video); sound (voice and sound: audio-speech, audio, audio-music, audio-sfx); documents (documents: document); links (web links: url, webpage); places (places: geo); data (numbers and data: structured, timeseries, event-stream, embedding); code (code: code); money (money: money); people (people: profile); dates (dates and events: schedule). A type id in parentheses also works, and stands for the id before it.

want.description: What the step should produce. One of: words (words: text, query, message, social-post); photos (photos and images: image, image-mask, 3d); video (video: video); sound (voice and sound: audio-speech, audio, audio-music, audio-sfx); documents (documents: document); links (web links: url, webpage); places (places: geo); data (numbers and data: structured, timeseries, event-stream, embedding); code (code: code); money (money: money); people (people: profile); dates (dates and events: schedule); done (something done: action:publish, action:message, action:money, action:world, action:software, action:browser, action:schedule, action:record, physical-item). A type id in parentheses also works, and stands for the id before it. “done” means the tool acts: it posts, sends, pays, books or changes something.

query.description: What the chain is for, in a few words, like “post clips to tiktok”. Both lists then hold only what the query fits, best first; without it, chains rank by how well the two tools fit the step, then by notability.

limit.description: Tools and chains to list of each kind, 1 to 10. Default 5.

tools.name: report_miss
tools.description: Tell EasyCanDo’s owner that search found no tool a step needed, so the catalog and search can improve. Call it only after the user agrees to send it. It sends what you give here: the search (up to 200 characters), what the step needed, and, if you want, a tool you expected and a note. Nothing else from the conversation. Reports are kept for 90 days. Up to 5 an hour.

query.description: The search that missed, as you sent it to search_tools.

need.description: What the step needed, in a sentence: “turn scanned receipts into a spreadsheet”.

expected.description: A tool you expected the catalog to have, by name or link, if any.

note.description: Anything else the owner should know, such as what search showed instead.
